name: A Crossed Acquired Pair Freezes Its Common Carrier
statement: In an ample two-layer family with common section $B$, suppose one wing acquires $\{x,y\}$ and the other acquires $\{x,z\}$, while $B$ shatters the three singletons. Then the projections of $B$ to $\{x,y\}$ and $\{x,z\}$ are uniquely punctured squares, the corresponding triples with the layer coordinate are minimal nonfaces with oppositely layered omitted traces, and every $x$-edge of $B$ has the same forced $y$- and $z$-values. Hence distinct distinguished $x$-edges are joined inside the connected $x$-carrier by a path of $\{x,t\}$-squares using neither partner direction.
proof: Projection preserves ampleness. Since $B$ shatters both singletons but not the pair, each two-coordinate projection has three concepts and is a uniquely punctured square by Sandwich equality. Shadow intersection makes the opposite wing omit the same trace, so the three-coordinate projection with the layer bit is a once-punctured cube and the triple is a minimal nonface. An $x$-edge using the omitted $y$- or $z$-value would realize the missing trace, forcing both partner values on every such edge. The anchor set of an $x$-carrier in an ample family is connected; with $y,z$ constant, every transport step uses another coordinate $t$ and corresponds to a full $\{x,t\}$-square.
